title: Aralo group file `_group.yaml` (format v0)
description: Describes one group, which is one folder of a library. The file is optional and so is every key in it: a folder without `_group.yaml`, or with an empty one, is a group named after the folder that inherits everything. Unknown keys at the top level and inside `defaults` are accepted and written back unchanged. Format v0 is pre-release and may change without a migration.
$comment: Mirrors `GroupFile`, `ScopeSpec` and `Defaults` in crates/aralo-snippet/src/group.rs. When the two disagree, the Rust code wins; please report it.

name.description: Display name. Absent or null: the folder name.

colour.description: Display colour, for example `"#3478F6"`. Stored as written; this version does not check the value. Quote it: an unquoted `#` starts a YAML comment.

icon.description: Display icon name. Stored as written; this version does not check the value.

enabled.description: `false` switches off this group and everything beneath it: its snippets, its sub-groups and their snippets. Absent or null: enabled, unless a group above it is disabled.

scope.description: The apps this group's snippets work in. Absent or null: inherit the parent group's scope. `{}`: everywhere, whatever the parent group says.

App scope. Entries are bundle IDs on macOS (executable names on Windows, later) and are compared without regard to ASCII case. Set `only` or `except`, never both. Unknown keys inside `scope` are accepted but, unlike elsewhere, are not written back.

only.description: The group works in these apps and nowhere else.

except.description: The group works everywhere but in these apps.

not.$comment: Rejected with `ConflictingScope`: both lists present and both non-empty.

defaults.description: Values this group's snippets and sub-groups inherit unless they set their own. Resolution order for each key: the snippet's own value, then the nearest group's `defaults`, then each parent group in turn, then the built-in default.

keep_delimiter.description: Re-insert the triggering delimiter after the expansion. Built-in default: `true`.

delimiters.description: Every character of this string is a delimiter, for example `" \t\n.,;"`. Use a double-quoted YAML string so that `\t` and `\n` are read as tab and newline. Group-level only: a snippet cannot set its own delimiter set. Built-in default: the engine's `DEFAULT_DELIMITERS`, listed in docs/format/matching.md.
